newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish minister sees no quick fuel-price rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish minister sees no quick fuel-price rise.

text.p: Poland will free its fuel prices over the next few months and not weeks, PAP news agency reported Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko as saying on Friday.
"I won't agree to a freeing of fuel prices when together with what's going on in international markets it would mean pushing prices upwards," PAP quoted Kolodko as saying.
"It's not a question of days or weeks but it's definitely a question of the next few months," added Kolodko, who was visiting an oil refinery in southeastern Poland.
Polish fuel prices are set by the finance ministry, which, despite rising world prices, does not want to allow domestic rises to avoid the strong inflationary effect their rise would create.
But refineries and distributors, facing official caps on fuel prices and high prices of crude oil, find production and sales increasingly less profitable.

On Thursday Poland's second largest refinery in Gdansk said it would cut monthly diesel fuel sales by 30 percent to 80,000 tonnes in September because imports were too costly after recent world oil price rises.
On Wednesday deputy industry minister Roman Czerwinski said Poland may have to use state reserves of diesel and introduce duty-free import quotas to offset shortages.
Czerwinski said duty-free import quotas for 300,000 tonnes of gasoline and 400,000 tonnes of diesel may be needed to stabilise the market unless world oil prices fall.
